title: Calling dotenv.config() results in a TypeError
publicBody:
Since upgrading from dotenv 14.2.0 to 14.3.0 I get the following error when calling `dotenv.config()`

CODE (foo.js):
```
...
import * as dotenv from "dotenv";
dotenv.config(); // line 20
...
```

ERROR:
```
$ yarn build
$ tslint -c tslint.json -p tsconfig.json --fix
$ tsc
$ node --es-module-specifier-resolution=node .
file:///..../foo.js:20
dotenv.config();
       ^

TypeError: dotenv.config is not a function
    at file:///..../foo.js:20:8
    at ModuleJob.run (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:185:25)
    at async Promise.all (index 0)
    at async ESMLoader.import (node:internal/modules/esm/loader:281:24)
    at async loadESM (node:internal/process/esm_loader:88:5)
    at async handleMainPromise (node:internal/modules/run_main:65:12)
```

Downgrading to 14.2.0 solves the error.
contractNotes: Restore public namespace import config() and parse() while preserving CommonJS/default imports, actual custom-file loading, existing environment handling, and returned error behavior. Independent assertions are API-level, no requirement to emit exact upstream statements. Fix production change is only lib/main.js.

title: # inside double quotes still treated as inline comment
publicBody:
v14.2.0
`SOME_KEY={"field1":"some value", "field2": "stops here#this is discarded"}`
When above line is parsed generates the following output
`SOME_KEY: {"field1":"some value", "field2": "stops here`
which in turns gives a SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input
contractNotes: Retain complete unquoted JSON strings containing a non-whitespace-preceded hash, as original issue reproduction requires, plus retain documented basic parsing/comment/quote/trim/Buffer/newline behavior. No new multiline, interpolation, hash-with-whitespace-inside-unquoted-JSON requirements. The historical patch explicitly specifies whitespace before inline comments; broad parser overhaul is not demanded.

title: Memory leak when using abort signals
publicBody: We have encountered a memory leak issue. After an extensive search for the source of the leak, it was found that it occurred in pMap. Upon reviewing the source code of your package, I discovered that you subscribe to the AbortSignal event but do not unsubscribe from it, which causes the memory leak.
contractNotes: Settled mapping must not keep AbortSignal event listeners; verify success, empty and skipped input, mapper and aggregate errors, shared-signal reuse, and active cancellation while preserving results/error identity and optional-signal behavior. Uses Node public getEventListeners API rather than monkeypatching implementation. Pre-aborted cleanup is deliberately not graded because the historical reference still adds a listener after already-aborted rejection.
